lines: Riley Chen
+1 (555) 010-7731 | riley.chen@example.com | example.com/in/riley-chen
Date of birth: 2 Nov 1996 | Nationality: American
EDUCATION
Northfield School of Management | MBA | Metro City, USA | Sep 2023 - Jun 2025
Lakeview University | B.A. in Economics | Lake City, USA | Sep 2014 - Jun 2018
EXPERIENCE
Harbor Payments | Associate Product Manager Intern | Metro City, USA | Jun 2024 - Aug 2024
- Improved checkout conversion by 35% after replacing the three-step flow with a one-page flow for all merchants.
- Wrote the requirements and success metrics for dispute self-service, aligning engineering, risk and support; the team shipped it two weeks ahead of plan.
- Interviewed 25 merchants and analysed six months of chargeback data to size annual chargeback losses at 1.1 million dollars, the business case that set the next quarter's roadmap priority.
- Ran weekly triage with engineering and support, closing 140 onboarding tickets over the summer and cutting the open-ticket queue by half.
- Measured the onboarding redesign by comparing merchants who opted into the new flow with those who stayed on the old one.
- Redesigned merchant onboarding around a single verification step, cutting median time to first payment from 9 days to 4 across 2,300 new merchants in the pilot region.
Crestline Logistics | Operations Analyst | Lake City, USA | Mar 2019 - Aug 2023
- Cut late deliveries from 11% to 7% by excluding weather-delayed shipments from the on-time calculation.
- Cut warehouse pick errors 30% at two sites by redesigning slotting rules with the floor supervisors and retraining 45 pickers on the new layout.
- Coordinated the quarterly S&OP review across sales, finance and operations and prepares the forecast pack for each meeting.
- Led the rollout of a route-planning tool to 3 depots, training 60 drivers and dispatchers and saving 1,800 driver hours a year.
PROJECTS
Campus Food Rescue App | Product Lead | Student Venture | Oct 2023 - Present
- Launched a surplus-food pickup app to 3,100 students with two dining halls, redistributing 9 tonnes of food that would have been thrown away in its first year.
- Launched pickup reminders after 60 user interviews showed students missed pickup windows; weekly active users grew from 400 to 1,150 over the following term.
- Set up a volunteer shift system with two dining halls, filling 95% of pickup slots each week and cutting staff cover shifts from 10 to 2 a week.
MBA Consulting Practicum | Team Lead | Regional Hospital Network | Jan 2024 - May 2024
- Held weekly working sessions with clinic managers on outpatient scheduling across the network.
- Patient intake at 4 clinics was mapped and the intake form was shortened, with the changes adopted by front-desk staff.
- Halved the time it takes a new merchant to receive a first payment, across 2,300 merchants, by redesigning onboarding.
SKILLS
Product: roadmapping, A/B testing, user interviews, requirements writing
Tools: Jira, Amplitude, Excel

items.says: Remove date of birth.
items.because: It is not relevant to your qualifications and can create avoidable age-bias concerns.

items.says: Remove nationality unless required for work authorization or compliance.
items.because: It is not relevant unless a specific application requires it.

items.says: Use the full professional LinkedIn URL and confirm profile consistency.
items.because: A complete and consistent profile is important.

items.says: Clarify whether the MBA is completed or in progress.
items.because: The dates end in June 2025, so the status should match your actual situation.

items.says: Add only the most relevant GPA, honors, coursework, leadership, or project details if strong.
items.because: Do not add generic coursework just to fill space.

items.says: Add concentration, honors, or relevant coursework only if it supports your target roles.
Define whether the 35% is a relative or percentage-point increase.
State the measurement period and size of the merchant or customer population.
Explain whether the improvement came from an A/B test, before-and-after, or other method.
Be cautious with 'for all merchants' as it sounds unusually broad and may invite questions about rollout scope and causality.
Distinguish your contribution from the result of the entire team.
Clarify whether the product actually launched and if there was an outcome after launch.
Clarify whether you owned the planning, coordination, or delivery process that affected the timing.
Add measurable effects on support volume, resolution time, or dispute completion if available.
items.because: Those would be more valuable than schedule performance alone.

items.says: Use a consistent currency format rather than spelling out the amount.
Clarify whether the figure represents total losses, preventable losses, or an estimate.
Explain the method used to produce the estimate if space permits.
items.because: Readers may question how interviews and six months of data led to an annual figure.

items.says: Specify whether the roadmap priority was approved, funded, or delivered.
Clarify whether you personally closed the tickets or coordinated their resolution.
Explain the significance of closing 140 onboarding tickets through resolution time, backlog age, or merchant impact.
items.because: 'Closing' could mean administrative closure rather than solving user problems.

items.says: Define the comparison period for 'cutting the open-ticket queue by half.'
Add the result of the measurement; currently only the evaluation method is described.
Address possible selection bias in comparing opt-in merchants to those who did not opt in.
items.because: That comparison may have selection bias.

items.says: Combine this bullet with the next onboarding bullet to connect evaluation method and result.
items.because: They are currently disconnected.

items.says: Clarify whether the reduction from 9 days to 4 days was measured against a baseline or control group.
Explain whether 2,300 merchants were part of a pilot, experiment, or full rollout.
Ensure the 'single verification step' claim is accurate if other onboarding requirements remained.
This bullet overlaps with the final bullet under the consulting practicum; keep it in only one place.
items.because: Duplication creates a credibility problem.

items.says: Do not present a lower late-delivery rate as an operational improvement if it resulted from changing the calculation rather than improving performance.
items.because: It is the biggest credibility problem in the resume.

items.says: Clearly distinguish metric-definition work from actual delivery improvement.
If you have a separate result showing improved performance after operational changes, use that instead.
Clarify the time period over which the 30% reduction was measured.
Indicate whether the reduction applied equally across both sites or to the combined total.
Tense is inconsistent: 'coordinated' is past tense, 'prepares' is present; make tense consistent with role dates.
Add the business consequence of the forecast pack or review.
items.because: Currently describes recurring responsibilities but gives no result.

items.says: Clarify your specific ownership rather than listing the meeting process alone.
Clarify whether the 1,800 annual driver hours are measured savings or a projected estimate.
Indicate the time period or baseline used to calculate the savings.
Include additional outcomes if the rollout improved route completion, fuel usage, overtime, or delivery performance.
Clarify whether the 9 tonnes were measured, estimated, or reported by the dining halls.
Make the timeframe consistent with the project dates; 'in its first year' may not align if the project is ongoing.
Distinguish between app reach and adoption; clarify whether 3,100 students used the app or had access.
Add adoption, retention, transaction, or completion rate if available.
items.because: That would make the launch evidence more meaningful.

items.says: State whether weekly active users increased directly after the reminder launch or over the entire term.
Explain whether the increase was measured against a control group, prior term, or before-and-after comparison.
Clarify that the 60 interviews generated the product decision but did not by themselves prove causality.
items.because: Interviews alone do not prove reminders caused user growth.

items.says: Avoid using 'launched' repeatedly across adjacent bullets unless each launch is a distinct milestone.
Clarify whether the 95% fill rate is an average, minimum, or peak.
Explain how staff cover shifts fell from 10 to 2 and over what period.
Clarify whether the reduction came from the volunteer system alone or other staffing changes.
Add what the sessions produced: agreement, implementation, redesign, or decision.
items.because: Currently activity-focused and needs an outcome.

items.says: Explain your role as team lead beyond facilitating meetings.
Add measurable changes in appointment access, wait times, staff workload, or utilization if available.
items.because: Those are more valuable than meeting frequency.

items.says: Avoid passive construction; clarify your personal role.
items.because: Passive voice hides what you did.

items.says: Quantify the form reduction if possible: number of fields, completion time, abandonment, or processing time.
Clarify how widely the new process was adopted and whether it produced a measurable result.
Ensure the healthcare context is accurate; do not imply patient outcomes if only administrative outcomes were measured.
Remove this bullet; it refers to merchants, duplicates the Harbor Payments accomplishment, and creates a credibility problem.
items.because: It does not match the hospital-network project and is a duplicate.

items.says: Retain only skills you can discuss concretely in an interview; add only the most valuable methods.
items.because: 'Roadmapping' and 'requirements writing' are broad.

items.says: Indicate your level of Excel proficiency if appropriate.
Consider adding tools actually used in the bullets, not just common ones.
Demonstrate how you used Jira and Amplitude, not just list them.
Use consistent spelling and style (e.g., 'analysed' vs. American spelling).
items.because: The resume is U.S.-oriented and should use one convention.

items.says: Use consistent number and currency formatting throughout.
Use past tense for completed roles and present tense only for ongoing work.
Consider putting Experience before Education if targeting product roles.
items.because: Experience contains stronger evidence.

items.says: Remove bullets that describe only a responsibility unless followed by a clear result.
Verify that every metric has a baseline, timeframe, population, and measurement method where those details affect credibility.
Keep the resume to one page if possible, but do not reduce readability by using very small type or tight spacing.
